picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 Tatum downplays beef Knicks change ring tune Cowboys not trading? 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

Questionable for this matchup are LB CJ Allen (ankle), LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), P Rigoberto Sanchez (foot), and CB Justin Walley (knee). Allen appeared on the injury report on Thursday and then did not practice on Friday. Boettcher was a non-participant on Friday as well. Potentially without these two, the Colts ' linebacker depth would be hampered. As a result, we could see Germaine Pratt elevated from the practice squad. Walley was limited the final two days after not practicing on Wednesday. If he can't go, we could see Kapena Gushiken in the slot, with Cam Taylor-Britt likely starting outside in Gardner's absence. away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns. away.headline: Colts sign WR Mecole Hardman, P Thomas Morstead to practice squad; release WR Eli Pancol from practice squad
away.blurb: Hardman Jr., 5-10, 187 pounds, has played in 82 career games (28 starts) in his time with the Buffalo Bills (2025-26), Green Bay Packers (2025), Kansas City Chiefs (2019-24) and New York Jets (2023). He has compiled 178 receptions for 2,302 yards (12.9 avg.) and 16 touchdowns. Hardman Jr. has tallied 26 carries for 190 yards (7.3 avg.) and three touchdowns. He has totaled 46 kickoff returns for 1,134 yards (24.7 avg.) and one touchdown as well as 91 punt returns for 823 yards (9.0 avg.) and one touchdown. Hardman Jr. has appeared in 15 postseason contests (four starts) and has tallied 28 receptions for 292 yards (10.4 avg.) and four touchdowns. He has also recorded 13 carries for 105 yards (8.1 avg.) and one touchdown. Hardman Jr. has collected 15 kickoff returns for 334 yards (22.3 avg.) and seven punt returns for 86 yards (12.3 avg.). He won Super Bowls LIV and LVIII with the Chiefs. Hardman Jr. was originally selected by Kansas City in the second round (56th overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft out of Georgia. As a rookie, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice (kick returner) and was named to the Pro Bowl (return specialist). His first name is pronounced MUH-cole. Morstead, 6-4, 225 pounds, has played in 272 career games in his time with the San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). He has registered 1,004 punts for 46,863 yards (46.7 avg./41.3 net avg.) with 374 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has also totaled 263 touchbacks on kickoffs. He has appeared in 18 postseason contests and has compiled 64 punts for 2,821 yards (44.1 avg./40.8 net avg.) with 22 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Morstead has tallied 16 touchbacks on kickoffs. He won Super Bowl XLIV with New Orleans. Morstead was originally selected by the Saints in the fifth round (164th overall) of the 2009 NFL Draft out of SMU. In 2012, he was an Associated Press Second Team All-Pro choice and was named to the Pro Bowl. Pancol, 6-3, 205 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on September 23, 2026. He participated in the Colts' 2026 offseason program and training camp. Pancol was originally signed to the team's practice squad on November 18, 2025. He spent time with the Jacksonville Jaguars during the 2025 offseason program and training camp after originally signing with the team as an undrafted free agent on April 28, 2025, out of Duke. home.headline: Vikings-Colts First Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets Mark H. Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

away.headline: Dolphins-Jets Injury Update: Bye Leaves Key Miami Questions Open
away.blurb: Miami's Week 6 bye prevents the Dolphins from issuing a conventional Friday game-status report, so no player should be labeled officially out or questionable for the Oct. 25 Jets game unless the club has made that designation. The week still produced several important health developments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea did not participate in Tuesday's voluntary practice after leaving the Cincinnati game with an ankle injury. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. Fantasy analyst Ian Hartitz also sounded unconvinced by the glove solution. “No reason to worry here. They ripped off one of the glove’s fingers! He’s fine! Everything is fine,” Hartitz wrote sarcastically . One fan expressed concern , writing, “So his throwing hand isn’t 100% healthy, which means he shouldn’t be playing.” Another fan imagined Carolina’s defenders enjoying the matchup. “Devin Lloyd and Will Lee stretching for some pick sixes this week,” the fan joked . home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. Mayfield missed the past three games with a dislocated right thumb, but returned to practice this week wearing a protective white glove designed to add support to the area. He said Thursday the thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to be able to play.” “It feels fine gripping it and throwing it,” Mayfield said. “It’s just the impact stuff. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. Bengals vs. Ravens bold predictions for AFC North clash in Week 7 Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Cincinnati Bengals , Ja'Marr Chase saved some money by appealing. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.headline: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson practices again, raising hopes for return vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Both Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley met with the media on Friday afternoon at the Ravens’ Owings Mills practice facility. By rule, teams must make their starting quarterback available to reporters at least once during the week leading up to a game. Having both quarterbacks available, though, was highly unusual. Lamar Jackson has found himself at the center of an injury-report controversy, and the Baltimore Ravens quarterback isn’t staying quiet about it. Jackson is still working his way back from an ankle issue, but he recently pushed back against Ian Rapoport’s report about its severity, saying his own trainers gave him a different diagnosis. Lamar Jackson Challenges Ian Rapoport’s Injury Report Jackson injured his left ankle during Baltimore’s Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans and missed the next two games. Rapoport had reported that the injury was neither a high-ankle nor a low-ankle sprain. Jackson, however, said the Ravens’ medical staff gave him a different diagnosis. When a reporter asked about the discrepancy, Jackson questioned Rapoport’s source while making it clear that he was going with what his own medical staff told him. “Rapoport said that? He part of the training staff?” Jackson asked. “So we can’t go off Ian Rapoport and his reporting. Somebody probably told him that too, though, so I can’t blame him. But nah, man, my staff told me it was a high-ankle sprain, so we’re going with what [head certified athletic trainer] Adrian [Dixon] told me.” Physical therapist Jeff Mueller said the situation showed how easily information can get lost or changed as it passes from sources to reporters and then to fans. He wrote on X , “Great reminder that telephone between (source) and NFL insider often relays wrong information, and then, we intake wrong information as audience. If it was initially reported as a high ankle sprain, no one would be surprised that Lamar Jackson has missed this much time.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Meanwhile, Ravens podcast host Samuel Njoku was fed up with the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback’s injuries, posting , “Always ‘misinformation and speculation’ when it comes to Lamar injuries.” Rob Pizzola saw Jackson’s response as a win for the medical staff and a tough moment for NFL reporters. He wrote , “Patient overrides the insider report with his own trainer’s diagnosis. Huge win for the medical community. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Eligible to Play vs. Ravens After NFL Reduces Discipline Upon Appeal
home.blurb: The Bills are on bye this week and will return to action on Nov. 1 in a marquee matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo has won back-to-back games after suffering its first loss of the season against the New England Patriots in Week 4. Buffalo Bills linebacker Sam Franklin Jr. will be eligible to play in Week 8 when the team returns from a bye after having his discipline reduced. Michael Signora, NFL senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday that Franklin's appeal of his one-game suspension was reduced to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct by hearing officer James Thrash. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Franklin was being suspended for one game due to "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" during Buffalo's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. Franklin was said to have spit on a Raiders player during an extra-point attempt late in the fourth quarter. In a post on Instagram after the league announced its discipline, Franklin denied any wrongdoing: "Not a dirty player what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone!" "As we said from the start, Sam did not and would never spit at an opponent, and there was no evidence that he did," Franklin's agents said in a statement . "We're glad the suspension was overturned and grateful to the hearing officer for a fair and thorough review. "It's unfortunate the league suspended Sam in the first place based on an unsupported accusation that received so much undeserved attention, and we hope the outcome is covered just as widely. We also hope the league takes a serious look at the opposing player's conduct, including striking Sam in the groin twice during the game. We're glad this is behind him, so Sam can get back to focusing on his teammates and next Sunday." Franklin was one of two Bills players disciplined for their actions during the Raiders game. C.J. Gardner-Johnson was suspended one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Officials flagged Gardner-Johnson for unsportsmanlike conduct and he was ejected from the game as a result of the incident. He issued an apology on social media following the Bills' win. Franklin is in his second season with the Bills after originally joining their practice squad in August 2025. He has appeared in 23 consecutive games since the start of last season. The 30-year-old Franklin has six combined tackles in six games in 2026. A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home For the New York Giants, it’s a matter of 3-2-1 … and hopefully no Illegal Contact. 2026’s Big Blue boasts Week 7’s weird record after dropping an entertaining outcome to… Kurt Boyer Updated Oct 23, 2026 6:13 PM EDT Al Bello/Getty Images Share this story For the New York Giants, it's a matter of 3-2-1 … and hopefully no Illegal Contact. 2026's Big Blue boasts Week 7's weird record after dropping an entertaining outcome to the New Orleans Saints, hoping to rebound against the host Houston Texans inside NRG Stadium at 1 p.m. ET this Sunday. Head coach Jim Harbaugh made a quarterback change with the Giants badly trailing the Saints. It was the Minnesota Vikings castoff JJ McCarthy who came in to relieve Jameis Winston, surprising spectators by leading New York to a valiant comeback bid without appearing as only the package QB, as McCarthy had done previously. McCarthy led the team to a red zone chance that could have tied the score with seconds remaining. The Giants recovered two straight onside kicks while turning a 34-10 deficit into a 34-27 final. McCarthy is clearly the Giants' starter in the imminent future. How is Harbaugh's new rehabilitation project going to fare against Houston, which limited Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence's accuracy in last weekend's 34-31 upset over the Jags in Florida? It can only be the hype that's making O/U lines rise. New York Giants at Houston Texans Predictions and Picks QB CJ Stroud and the Houston Texans aced their October road trip, going 2-0 with victories in Tennessee and Jacksonville. But the reason the Texans are 2-4 is that Space City has not matched that success at home this season. Counting exhibition contests, fans have yet to see the Texans win at home in the 2026-27 campaign. Houston also had some troubling injury woes crop up in its Week 6 win, a prognosticators' clue that the Texans' two-game winning streak may not be extended. Two of the Texans' key defensive starters may have gone down with concussions on the same Sunday. Houston linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and safety Reed Blankenship, per Josh Buckhalter at Yahoo Sports , each “exited the (Jacksonville) game during the second quarter” to undergo concussion protocol. The weakening of a defense that had been carrying the team via opponents' low rush totals is a reason handicappers have given the Giants a 10-point edge over the Texans on the road this weekend. That's probably a wide point spread for a New York club that's down to its third QB already, reflective of the phenomenal amount of hype around any potential Giants winning season. away.headline: New York Giants' Chauncey Golston out for season with neck injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Golston, placed on injured reserve (IR) earlier this month, is confirmed out for the year. The 28-year-old was hurt during New York’s Week 4 win over the Arizona Cardinals and did not return. He finished the game with two tackles before exiting. The former third-round pick out of Iowa had carved out a meaningful role in his second season with the Giants after signing a three-year, $18 million deal as a free agent in 2025. He appeared in each of the team’s first four games, working as a rotational piece on both base downs and in pass-rush packages while lining up at multiple spots along the defensive front. This article originally appeared on Giants Wire: New York Giants' Chauncey Golston out for season with neck injury The New York Giants will be without defensive lineman Chauncey Golston for the rest of the 2026 season after he suffered a neck injury. Early indications pointed to a long-term issue. Although Golston sought a second opinion in hopes of a better outcome, he will not be activated from IR. Golston’s versatility stemmed from his time in Dallas, where he developed as a flexible edge and interior contributor. His absence further thins an already taxed defensive line group. The Giants have also lost linebacker Tremaine Edmunds to a growing list of season-ending injuries after he suffered a torn chest muscle. New York will now need remaining defensive linemen and recent roster additions to absorb a larger share of snaps as the team moves through the middle of its schedule.

away.headline: Report: Giants' Tremaine Edmunds out for season with shoulder injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The injury marks the latest setback for a Giants defense that has been forced to reshuffle personnel repeatedly. With Burns already sidelined and now Edmunds out, the linebacking corps faces significant challenges in maintaining its effectiveness down the stretch. This article originally appeared on Giants Wire: Report: Giants' Tremaine Edmunds out for season with shoulder injury The New York Giants received another devastating injury blow on Friday with news that linebacker Tremaine Edmunds suffered a season-ending shoulder injury, reports Dan Duggan of The Athletic . The news compounds an already dire situation for a team that has already lost quarterback Jaxson Dart and outside linebacker Brian Burns, along with several other contributors, for the remainder of the year. Edmunds, one of the Giants’ top free-agent additions, had been a constant presence on defense, logging every snap while helping ease rookie linebacker Arvell Reese into the NFL. Micah McFadden is expected to step into Edmunds’ role and start alongside Reese. Head coach John Harbaugh has previously indicated the Giants view themselves as having three starting inside linebackers, giving McFadden the opportunity to seize a larger role in the middle of the defense. Edmunds’ absence removes a veteran presence and a key communicator from a unit already stretched thin by injuries. His consistency had provided stability next to the developing Reese, and his loss forces the Giants to lean more heavily on younger or less-proven options as they navigate the second half of the season. McFadden’s ability to fill the void will be closely watched as the Giants attempt to manage the mounting absences and stay competitive.

away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. picks.blurb: Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction for NFL Week 7 (Expect Low-Scoring Game With Denver’s Offense Struggling) Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Can Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos finally get going on offense? Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. A week ago, the discussion surrounding this team centered on the job security of general manager Monti Ossenfort, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The season appeared to be spiraling toward a similar finish to last year's 3-14 record. Now, it suddenly feels as if Mike LaFleur has his operation on the right track in Year 1 as head coach. The vibes are good again. Week 7 offers a unique test of those vibes. The Denver Broncos come to town, armed with an elite defense and a miserable offense. The Cardinals offense, in turn, will aim to show that it can hang with the best. The Cardinals defense will aim to avoid a deflating comedown after last week's performance. (Kiyoshi Mio/Imagn Images) 1 / 20 Arizona Cardinals visit NFC West foe Los Angeles Rams in Week 6 Arizona Cardinals visit NFC West foe Los Angeles Rams in Week 6 It's a fascinating matchup. Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4) Time/site: 1:05 p.m. MST, State Farm Stadium, Glendale, Arizona. TV: CBS . Radio: 98.7. Last time they played: It's been four years since the Cardinals faced the Broncos. They lost 24-15 in one of the final games of the Kliff Kingsbury era. These rosters have more familiarity, though, from a joint practice in August 2025, in which the Broncos had the clear upper hand on both sides of the ball. Series history: The Cardinals are 1-10-1 all-time against Denver, their worst record against any opponent. The lone win came in 2010, when John Skelton beat Kyle Orton late in what was a lost season for both teams. Coaching matchup On offense, LaFleur will have to find solutions for Vance Joseph, the former Cardinals defensive coordinator who has seen his star rise since joining Denver in 2023. On the other side of the ball, Broncos head coach Sean Payton recently took playcalling duties back from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, who was seen as one of the league's ascendant young coaches entering the season. Rallis will aim to exploit the disarray. Arizona will win if… Its defense pressures Bo Nix: Nix has been bad in general this season, but he's been especially poor against pressure, with eight turnover-worthy plays on 80 dropbacks. That's one of the worst rates in the league, so the Cardinals will aim to make him uncomfortable, as they did with Matthew Stafford last week. Its run game improves: The Cardinals don't need to score 30 points to win this game, but they do need to find some offensive answers. Even without Jeremiyah Love , that likely starts with getting a sputtering rushing attack going. Denver's otherwise vaunted defense ranks 25th in yards per carry allowed. LaFleur finds a way to unlock Michael Wilson: In two games since Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded, Wilson has just eight catches for 62 yards on 14 targets. Compare that to last season, when Wilson averaged 97.2 yards per game when Harrison was out. It won't be easy against Pat Surtain, but to find an explosive element, this offense needs to get Wilson more involved. Denver will win if… The turnover machine keeps rolling: The Broncos defense has sacrificed some down-to-down efficiency this season to become a turnover machine. After ranking 27th in takeaways last year, they rank third this year, with 10 in six games. As underdogs, the Cardinals can't afford to give the ball away in this one. It leans into man coverage: The Cardinals have struggled mightily against man coverage this season but, for some reason, the Rams shied away from those looks last week. It seems like an easy button to press for a Broncos secondary that has the talent to take away Trey McBride and Michael Wilson one-on-one. Its defense stops the Cardinals' three-tight end sets: The Cardinals offense has one clear matchup advantage in this game. They use 13 personnel (one RB, three TEs) at the highest rate in the league. The Broncos defense, meanwhile, has been a bottom-three unit against those looks. That mismatch could enable the Cardinals offense to find more success than expected in this game. Mike LaFleur on Vance Joseph's Broncos defense: "They're very smart, they're very well coached. I have as much respect for VJ as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. … It's got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverages. And that's a credit to them." Sean Payton on the Cardinals defense, after their performance against the Rams: "This is a pressure defense. They give you some looks where they were problematic for the Rams. They were able to take a really good offense and a good quarterback and put them out of rhythm. So we're going to have to have the right answers." By the numbers 1 — Denver's strength of schedule ranking so far this season. The Cardinals rank third. Both these teams may be better than their records indicate. 3.2 — The Cardinals' points per drive when they get at least one first down. That ranks 10th in the league. But they go three-and-out at a top-five rate in the league, holding their offense back. 6.0 — Nix's average depth of target, the lowest in the league. Yet, his time to throw is the sixth-longest in the league. He is neither getting the ball in his playmakers' hands quickly nor pushing the ball downfield. It's a bad combination. 18.7 — Points per game allowed by the Broncos since the start of the 2024 season. No defense has been better over that span. 36.1% — The Cardinals' blitz rate in Week 6. In the first five weeks, that number was 25.6%, a bottom-10 rate in the league. Who will win and why Broncos 24, Cardinals 20: The Cardinals offense matches up surprisingly well with this vaunted Broncos defense, while Denver's own offensive struggles could open the door to another Arizona upset. Still, the Broncos' talent advantage gives them a slight edge. This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Cardinals vs Broncos prediction. Can Arizona pull off another upset?

away.headline: Pat Surtain injury: Latest updates for Broncos cornerback
away.blurb: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain went down with a non-contact ankle injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers . He was ruled out in the third quarter. Broncos CB Pat Surtain questionable for Week 7 Denver's injury report for Sunday's game against Arizona has cornerback Pat Surtain officially listed as questionable . If he can't play, Jahdae Barron will likely be the next man up. Despite returning to practice on Wednesday, Pat Surtain seems more likely to return in Week 8 against the Chiefs, according to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video . We'll see how the week goes for PS2. Pat Surtain might not return in Week 7 In an updated report on Pat Surtain's status, James Palmer of Prime Video clarified that PS2's injury was not a non-contact injury — it actually happened one play before the cornerback went down on the field. Palmer also reported that " [i]t might be tough " for Surtain to return to action in Week 7, suggesting PS2 might be more likely to return in Week 8. Pat Surtain ruled out for Week 6; there's hope for possible Week 7 return Pat Surtain has been ruled out for a Thursday Night Football clash with the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, but there is hope he might be able to return against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, according to KUSA-TV's Mike Klis . Pat Surtain avoids IR; ruled out for Week 5 ESPN's Adam Schefter said on Altitude Sports Radio that his guess is that Pat Surtain will land on injured reserve , which would rule the cornerback out for at least four games. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported this morning that Pat Surtain is expected to miss time, but it's not believed to be season-ending. "You hope it is just a couple weeks, maybe it ends up in an IR stint, but not expected to be season-ending," Rapoport said . If Surtain is placed on injured reserve, he would have to sit out at least four games. Broncos CB Pat Surtain ruled out Broncos cornerbacks Pat Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), who were both originally listed as questionable to return, have been announced as ruled out for the rest of today's game. Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron are the two outside cornerbacks with Ja'Quan McMillian playing in the slot. Behind them on Denver's depth chart , the Broncos also have Kris Abrams-Draine. With PS2 sidelined, the team is down to four healthy cornerbacks on the active roster. Update : Moss (ribs) was announced as questionable to return after halftime, so Denver now has Barron and Abrams-Draine starting at the two outside cornerback spots. Surtain was down on the field for a few moments before being helped off by two people, walking slowly into the locker room. Surtain was replaced on defense by cornerback Jahdae Barron, the team's first-round pick in last year's NFL draft. Barron played across from Riley Moss with Ja'Quan McMillian continuing to play in the slot. Surtain had totaled four tackles in the first half before leaving the game. away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. home.headline: Latest on if RB Jeremiyah Love will play for Cardinals in Week 7
home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur announced the news in his press conference on Friday, Oct. 23, ahead of the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos. This marks the second consecutive game that Love has missed as the Cardinals, following a nagging ankle injury that limited his explosiveness in recent weeks. In addition to Love, LaFleur ruled out defensive tackle Walter Nolen, safety Andrew Wingard and right guard Jon Gaines. Nolen, the Cardinals’ 2025 first-round pick, injured his ankle in the third quarter of last week’s win over the Rams . He returned to the game but came up limping after a snap late in the fourth quarter and did not return. Gaines is the newest addition to the injury report, as he suffered an ankle injury in practice on Thursday, Oct. 22. “Enough to keep him out for this week,” LaFleur said. The same goes for defensive lineman Darius Robinson, who was downgraded to questionable with a back injury on Thursday. LaFleur said that the situation is “similar” with cornerback Max Melton, who was limited on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. When asked, LaFleur said the Cardinals have not discussed placing Love on injured reserve. In Love's absence, the Cardinals will once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to lead their backfield. In Week 6, Allgeier finished with 18 carries for 38 yards, while Knight took 15 carries for 80 yards. Both players saw two targets, while Allgeier led in snap share, 56% to 44%. LaFleur described Allgeier as more of the Cardinals’ third-down back, whereas Knight’s role is more on first and second downs. Last week, Allgeier played on 10 of 15 third downs. On first and second down, Allgeier had 29 snaps to Knight’s 26. “(Allgeier) is extremely smart, so he's very beneficial for us on third downs, with the protection schemes, with his firmness, in terms of picking up pressures,” LaFleur said. “… So he provides that skill set for us. He can still do what we need on first and second down, but that's where Bam ends up coming in and doing a lot of that work on first and second down.” LaFleur said that the Cardinals do not expect Nolen to be placed on injured reserve, but he left the door more open there than he did with Love. “Don't expect, but as I've learned through seven weeks of the job, I expect anything,” LaFleur said. “But I just answer it with him; he's no different than all the other guys. Not expecting it, but there are setbacks. These are human bodies.” Wingard, meanwhile, will miss his third consecutive game after suffering a knee injury against the Giants in Week 4. The Cardinals have multiple options to fill his void at safety, with Wydett Williams and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson both now healthy. They could also play cornerback Garrett Williams in that spot, as they did last week. The Cardinals will turn to 2025 sixth-round pick Hayden Conner in Gaines’ absence. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. Packers Wire staff predictions: Week 7 vs. Lions Zach Kruse, Brandon Carwile, Mark Oldacres and Brennen Rupp, Packers Wire Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:08 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers are headed to Detroit to face the rival Lions on Sunday at Ford Field. Matt LaFleur's team has won three straight games after a 1-2 start and will attempt to beat the Lions for the third straight time overall and third time in four years at Ford Field. Here's how the staff at Packers Wire believes the Week 7 showdown with the Lions will go down: Zach Kruse: Packers 30, Lions 27 (4-2) I went back and forth on this prediction, weighing how well the Packers are playing defensively and the volume of explosive plays produced during the three-game win streak against a rested, talented Lions team featuring legitimate playmakers on both sides and a high-scoring offense. Plus, the impact of the environment inside Ford Field. The difference maker? The troubles of the Lions' defense, especially against the pass. The corners are struggling and Brian Branch isn't going to solve every problem. It's just difficult to envision the Lions being the team to get a stop in a big spot. This is a huge game in terms of early-season playoff positioning, especially considering how good all four teams in the NFC North appear to be at this point, so exiting Ford Field with a win would be huge. I'm expecting a back-and-forth game with plenty of explosive plays on both sides. The guess: the Lions tie it late, but Jordan Love gets into Trey Smack's range and the rookie walks it off for the Packers. Brandon Carwile: Packers 28, Lions 23 (4-2) Green Bay swept Detroit in the regular-season series in 2025 after being swept in 2024. The Lions have a ton of offensive firepower and are tied for first in points per game, while the Packers are allowing an average of 11.3 points during their three-game win streak. Jahmyr Gibbs poses a significant challenge, but hopefully Green Bay learned something from what Bijan Robinson did to them in Week 3. I don't expect much defense in this game. The Packers have done an outstanding job generating takeaways, but Detroit has just one turnover in five games. There's a good chance this one comes down to who can score more points, and Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are the most productive pass-catching duo in the league facing a Lions defense that is dead last in passing yards allowed per game. Mark Oldacres: Lions 31, Packers 28 (3-3) Green Bay's offensive has been productive enough to secure three straight wins but there were warning signs against Dallas, as the offensive line started to struggle again and points were left on the field due to drops. It remains to be seen if there are any changes on the offensive line, whether Josh Jacobs plays, and how impactful either of those changes are. On the other side of the ball, Jonathan Gannon's defense has been the more consistent contributor in the 4-2 start, but after passing the test of a talented Cowboys offense, they face an even more difficult challenge on the road in Detroit. It is tough to see them slowing down a Lions attack which can do damage on the ground through Jahmyr Gibbs, or through the air with Jared Goff — who is yet to throw an interception — as well as his multiple weapons. The Packers may need to win a shootout to come out on top, and there are enough reasons to think they will make one too many mistakes on offense for that to happen. Brennen Rupp: Packers 27, Lions 24 (4-2) This article originally appeared on Packers Wire: Packers Wire staff predictions: Week 7 vs. Lions
