High Stakes in Motown: Three Bold Predictions for Lions vs. Packers (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 23, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The classic NFC North rivalry reignites this Sunday at Ford Field in a clash carrying massive divisional implications. The Detroit Lions return home fresh off their bye week seeking to re-establish dominance in the North, while Jordan Love and the red-hot Green Bay Packers roll into town riding high momentum. Extra rest gives Dan Campbell's coaching staff two full weeks to scheme, but Matt LaFleur's offense has been operating with surgical precision. When these two powerhouse rosters collide, subplots will fly. Here are three bold predictions for Sunday's showdown. 1. Jahmyr Gibbs Out-Gains Green Bay's Entire Rushing Attack The Packers have leaned heavily on Jordan Love's arm, but their ground game has yielded inconsistent results throughout the early stretch of the season. Conversely, Detroit's dynamic backfield partner Jahmyr Gibbs comes into this contest thoroughly rested and ready to explode. Drew Petzing will feature Gibbs heavily in both the running and short-passing games to negate Green Bay's aggressive pass rush. Expect Gibbs to turn limited touches into game-breaking plays, accumulating over 130 total scrimmage yards on his own, out-gaining the Packers' team rushing output by the final whistle. 2. Aidan Hutchinson Hits a Career High in Single-Game Pressures Detroit's defensive anchor Aidan Hutchinson has been relentless up front. With the extra rest enabling him to rush at full throttle, Hutchinson faces a Green Bay offensive line that will be forced into passing situations if Detroit grabs an early lead. The prediction: Hutchinson completely disrupts Green Bay's passing rhythm, generating at least eight total quarterback pressures and logging 2.5 sacks on Jordan Love. His motor off the edge will keep Ford Field roaring and force Love into uncomfortable platform throws under pressure. 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Xavier McKinney Trade Game-Changing Playmaking This match features a high-stakes duel between elite stars: Detroit's top wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and Green Bay's ball-hawking safety Xavier McKinney. St. Brown will find his usual rhythm in the slot, hauling in double-digit receptions and at least one touchdown. However, McKinney won't leave Detroit empty-handed. Expect McKinney to jump an intermediate route for a critical second-half interception, setting up a nail-biting, fourth-quarter finish between two teams that refuse to give an inch. Divisional matchups coming off a bye week often turn into instant classics, and this one is going to be nothing short of that. While Green Bay enters Ford Field with plenty of heat, Detroit's fresh legs and hyper-aggressive offensive design should prove just enough to secure a thrilling victory at home. I expect this one to be back and forth until the final whistle.

picks.headline: Predictions: Lions vs. Green Bay Packers

Story by Detroit News Predictions: Lions vs. Green Bay Packers Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nolan Bianchi, Richard Silva, John Niyo and Bob Wojnowski of The Detroit News offer predictions for Sunday's game between the Lions and Green Bay Packers at Ford Field in Detroit (4:25 p.m., Fox/97.1 FM ). ▶ Nolan Bianchi: The Packers' receiving weapons feel like a natural place to start against a Lions secondary hoping to string two solid performances together: Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should terrify Detroit . But despite Green Bay's offensive line playing better of late, the Lions' defensive line does have an advantage there, and the big question is whether they can actually get to Jordan Love on high-leverage downs to get off the field. Offensively, Lions coordinator Drew Petzing is really starting to find his groove, and Jared Goff has played mistake-free football through five games ; Detroit's run game also has the advantage against Green Bay's run defense. I still think the Lions can outscore anybody in the league, and I'm expecting Detroit's defensive front to help get the occasional stop. Pick: Lions, 34-31 Packers receiver Matthew Golden is sixth in the NFL in receiving yards with 501. ▶ John Niyo: A fast start would go a long way for the Lions in this one. Green Bay has scored first in all six of its games, while Detroit has managed just 10 first-quarter points total this season. But regardless of how this game starts, the Lions know they'll have to finish drives with touchdowns the way they did in Arizona. Because while the Packers' run game isn't much of a threat, the explosive plays in the pass game are and we all know that's an area where the Lions have struggled mightily. It'll be interesting to see how a new-look offensive line performs with Cade Mays making his debut at center. Green Bay's blitzing paid off last week against Dallas, but if the Lions diagnose things right, there's a chance to cash in for Jared Goff & Co. Pick: Lions, 31-28 ▶ Richard Silva: The Packers haven't been able to effectively run the ball, and even with Josh Jacobs making his season debut, I don't expect them to get back on track against a Lions defense that's proven capable of bottling up opposing backs. But the Packers, winners of their last three games, have found success regardless of their poor rushing performance, relying on a defense that puts pressure on quarterbacks and, more importantly for this matchup, an explosive offense. The Lions have allowed 23 passing plays of at least 20 yards through five games. The Packers rank fourth in 20-yard passes on offense. That's where the game will be won or lost. Pick: Packers, 34-28 ▶ Bob Wojnowski: The energy should be bubbling for this one, the Lions' first NFC North clash against a team that has given them problems lately. The Packers have won two of the last three at Ford Field, and come in on a roll. Green Bay's pass-heavy offense might get a running boost with the return of Josh Jacobs. But make no mistake, Jordan Love will be heaving deep and often to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The Lions lead the league in sacks, and they'll need to get to Love before he gets to pick apart their lowest-ranked pass defense. Brian Branch returns as the secondary's leader and could make an immediate impact. Jared Goff is playing as well as ever, without an interception, and he'll be tested by a Packers defense that piles up takeaways. A lot of strength-versus-weakness matchups here, and the Lions' pass rush against Green Bay's depleted offensive line will be the difference. Pick: Lions, 30-24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Predictions: Lions vs. Green Bay Packers

away.headline: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. home.headline: Packers Hit With Brutal Injury News Ahead of Massive Showdown Against Lions
home.blurb: The 3–2 Detroit Lions will take on the 4–2 Green Bay Packers this Sunday in an important NFC North divisional matchup. Detroit has already announced that Brian Branch will play and Cade Mays will start at center. Return man DeAndre Carter was also elevated from the practice squad to the active roster and will handle punt and kick returns for the Lions. Detroit released a nearly clean injury report, with only Mays and Branch listed as questionable. However, both players are expected to play barring a setback. Green Bay has suffered numerous season-ending injuries heading into this matchup, an numerous players being placed on injured reserved. Currently on IR is starting wide receiver Jayden Reed, return specialist and wide receiver Skyy Moore, starting offensive tackle Zach Tom, starting defensive tackle Javon Hargrave, starting linebacker Edgerrin Cooper, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons and, most recently, starting linebacker Zaire Franklin was just ruled out. Meanwhile, wide receiver Bo Melton remains questionable with a back injury, starting guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee injury, and starting cornerback Benjamin St. Juste is questionable with a hamstring injury. Green Bay will welcome one addition to its lineup, as Josh Jacobs has been removed from the commissioner's exempt list and is expected to make his season debut for the Packers. Quarterback Jordan Love was previously listed on the injury report with a back injury but has since been removed and is good to go for Sunday. Matthew Golden, who has been dealing with a shoulder injury, and Christian Watson, who has been dealing with an ankle injury, are also expected to play. Detroit appears to have a significant advantage in terms of overall health heading into Sunday's contest. It is rare to see the Lions this healthy at this point in the NFL season, especially coming off their bye week. However, Detroit cannot afford to assume Green Bay's injuries will be enough to slow down its divisional rival. The Packers just defeated the Dallas Cowboys, holding them to 13 points, with Dallas scoring their second touchdown in garbage time late in the fourth quarter. After losing two of their first three games, the Packers have found their stride, winning their last three matchups against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Chicago Bears and Cowboys. Detroit, meanwhile, enters the matchup refreshed after its bye week and will look to take advantage of its relatively healthy roster as it prepares for its first divisional game of the season.

Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Los Angeles Rams fans will make the drive up I-15 this weekend for a team that badly needs a road win. The Rams are 2-4 after an 18-16 loss to Arizona, they've lost Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, and Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders are waiting at Allegiant Stadium. Sean McVay has said the Rams' depth can handle it for now. "It's significant when you don't have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust," McVay said Monday . Los Angeles is a 4.5-point favorite against a Raiders team on a three-game skid, and the Rams have a clear path back from 2-4 if three things break their way. Byron Young sacks Kirk Cousins twice Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Los Angeles Rams linebacker Byron Young (0) and safety Kamren Kinchens (5) sack Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) during the first half at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Byron Young has 29 pressures, sixth among 115 edge defenders, and his 22 hurries lead the position, according to PFF . He has only four sacks, though, and the Rams have just eight as a team despite one of the league's best pressure rates. They turn pressure into sacks just under 10% of the time, second-worst in the NFL, and we called the pressure-to-sack gap the first fix before Cousins this week. Cousins has thrown 14 touchdown passes against five interceptions, and he's been sacked eight times. He threw 41 passes in the 33-30 loss to Buffalo, and the Raiders run for only 79.2 yards per game, 30th in the league, so the dropbacks will come. Young finishes two of his pressures this time. Kyren Williams scores twice on 20 carries Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) is tackled by Arizona Cardinals linebacker Jack Gibbens (50) in the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn ImagesJayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Kyren Williams averages 4.9 yards per carry, but he got a season-low 10 carries against Arizona, and his frustration has put McVay's offense under scrutiny . He has 393 rushing yards, four rushing touchdowns and 30 catches. Las Vegas allows 134.3 rushing yards per game, 28th in the league, and Maxx Crosby is the reason to keep Matthew Stafford from dropping back 40 times. Crosby has 35 pressures, second among edge defenders, per PFF , and Stafford has no scramble yards to fall back on. Nakobe Dean has three forced fumbles, so Williams has to hold on, but he gets 20 carries and scores twice. Quentin Lake intercepts Cousins Sep 27, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake (37) defends against a pass intended for Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton (14) in the first half at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Quentin Lake has a 91.6 coverage grade, the best among safeties, and seven passes defensed through Week 5, according to PFF . He added an interception against Arizona. Cousins leans on Brock Bowers, who has 382 yards in four games, and Tre Tucker, who caught two touchdown passes against the Bills. Bowers does his damage over the middle, which is where Lake lives. The Rams' pass defense ranks second at 167 yards allowed per game, and Lake picks off Cousins in a win that gets Los Angeles back to 3-4. McVay knows the margins have been thin. The Rams have lost three one-score games, and his fourth-down calls backfired against Arizona. "We've had some really critical errors at really unfortunate times, but that's what our narrative has been for this year," he said after that loss. A clean game in Las Vegas would start changing it. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams could be without wide receiver Puka Nacua on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. Nacua was officially listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report after injuring his calf on Thursday . Also listed as questionable was cornerback Trent McDuffie, who did not practice on Friday. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has officially been ruled out. Nacua was a surprise addition to the injury report on Thursday after he left practice with an apparent calf injury. He did not practice on Friday and will be a game-time decision. According to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport , Nacua’s calf injury is only minor, but his status is up in the air for Sunday’s game. Rams head coach Sean McVay talked about Nacua’s injury in more detail in his media availability. Landman being ruled out would imply that he didn’t pass through the concussion protocol this week. With Landman unable to go, McVay noted on Friday that the team would bring up linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad, who they signed two weeks ago. McDuffie missing his fourth consecutive practice with a groin injury certainly isn’t a good sign. McVay didn’t provide much of an update on McDuffie, only that he was questionable. McDuffie did work off to the side to an extent during the media portion of practice. The Raiders will be relatively healthy heading into Sunday’s game against the Rams. After being limited on Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, tight end Brock Bowers was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and was not given an injury designation. Tonka Hemingway was also cleared. With that said, the Raiders will be without wide receiver Dont’e Thornton and tight end Carter Runyon. Running back Mike Washington’s status is also up in the air for Sunday. Washington has been used alongside Ashton Jeanty this season and has averaged 4.9 yards per carry. He did not participate in practice the last two days and is listed as questionable. home.headline: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email 📮 Editorial Board endorsements ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. The person spoke on the condition of anonymity because the signing has not been announced. The 31-year-old White returns for what would be a third stint in Buffalo

This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "The Chiefs, who’ve never fielded a top-15 rushing attack during Mahomes’ time as a starter, rank second with an average of 159.8 ground yards per game," Kownack wrote. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. Chiefs at Seahawks SNF: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction This is technically the second meeting between these two teams this year, following an ugly preseason tie in August that featured mostly second and third-string players. Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid watches play against the Seattle Seahawks during the game at Arrowhead Stadium. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 52.8%, Seahawks 46.8%. While Seattle boasts one of the best home-field advantages in the sport, the matchup predictor still gives the undefeated Chiefs a slight edge to maintain their perfect record. Chiefs on SI's Take Usually, the matchup predictor closely mirrors what traditional betting lines are forecasting. However, that isn't the case for this contest. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. Unlike some of their past opponents, Patrick Mahomes will make them pay. Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is
away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is Skip to content Chiefs coaches have fielded questions all week about the return, and they don't expect it to get in the way of the task at hand. Their description of Walker was simple: Level-headed. His comments throughout the week reflect just that. Walker says he's treating this like any other week. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy never returned to face a former team as a reigning world champion. He did face his former team as a player, though. The San Diego Chargers drafted Bieniemy in the 1991 NFL Draft, and he eventually played for the Cincinnati Bengals. Bieniemy didn't see the Chargers until Week 2 of the 1996 season. He had only two touches in that game: one carry for a 7-yard loss and a 9-yard reception. Regardless of the stat line, the experience gave Bieniemy insight into the emotions Walker could be feeling on Sunday night. Walker's RBs coach, DeMarco Murray, has also been through the same thing as a player. He faced the Dallas Cowboys as a divisional rival twice with the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2015 NFL season. Walker insists he won't make this matchup bigger than what it is. “It was mainly me and EB talking about how he went to a former team and how he felt about stuff, and you know, just giving me pointers on stuff like that,” Walker said. “But you just can't make it bigger than what it is. You know, I'm not the only one on this team. Everybody's going out there to play a game. I don't feel like it should be just about me.” That's the mentality of a true team player, and that outlook is part of what has made Walker's integration into Kansas City so seamless. He simply gets it. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is
home.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker refuses to make his return to Seattle in Week 7 to face the Seahawks any bigger than it is Skip to content Chiefs coaches have fielded questions all week about the return, and they don't expect it to get in the way of the task at hand. Their description of Walker was simple: Level-headed. His comments throughout the week reflect just that. Walker says he's treating this like any other week. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy never returned to face a former team as a reigning world champion. He did face his former team as a player, though. The San Diego Chargers drafted Bieniemy in the 1991 NFL Draft, and he eventually played for the Cincinnati Bengals. Bieniemy didn't see the Chargers until Week 2 of the 1996 season. He had only two touches in that game: one carry for a 7-yard loss and a 9-yard reception. Regardless of the stat line, the experience gave Bieniemy insight into the emotions Walker could be feeling on Sunday night. Walker's RBs coach, DeMarco Murray, has also been through the same thing as a player. He faced the Dallas Cowboys as a divisional rival twice with the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2015 NFL season. Walker insists he won't make this matchup bigger than what it is. “It was mainly me and EB talking about how he went to a former team and how he felt about stuff, and you know, just giving me pointers on stuff like that,” Walker said. “But you just can't make it bigger than what it is. You know, I'm not the only one on this team. Everybody's going out there to play a game. I don't feel like it should be just about me.” That's the mentality of a true team player, and that outlook is part of what has made Walker's integration into Kansas City so seamless. He simply gets it. home.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. home.blurb: NFL Fans Demand 'Investigation' Into Philadelphia Eagles' Medical Staff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Andrew Holleran Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Eagles are likely to be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, as he's being put on blood thinners, the team announced on Monday. Hurts missed this past Sunday's game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. "Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the team announced. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery." Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Hurts stayed up for about 36 hours straight before that game, after being diagnosed. "How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? After initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, doctors told him not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, throwing for 220 yards and a TD," he reported.
